fact: Fraternite Matin reports the BCEAO officially launched the PI-SPI interoperable instant payment platform on 30 September 2025, with 80 institutions already connected and connection mandatory for all UEMOA financial institutions from 30 June 2026.
Fraternite Matin reports the BCEAO's PI-SPI instant payment platform covers banks, microfinance, e-money and payment institutions across the UEMOA, Cote d'Ivoire's union.

The BCEAO granted licence EME.CI.025/2025 to Djogana Pay, its Peya Pay e-money, as the fourth electronic-money institution in Cote d'Ivoire, activities being possible only after central bank approval.
The BCEAO announced that public Treasuries are being connected to its PI-SPI interoperable instant-payment platform, with Cote d'Ivoire's already in service.
Launch Base Africa reports the BCEAO runs PI-SPI, the shared instant payment platform through which interoperable e-money transfers have had to route since 2 November 2026, covering Cote d'Ivoire.

BiFinances says the BCEAO's PI-SPI platform, launched 30 September 2025, runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and that on 2 April 2026 the BCEAO counted 80 connected participants including nine e-money institutions.
BiFinances reports Wave announced on 6 November 2026 that its customers in Cote d'Ivoire can use the BCEAO's regional PI-SPI platform from its app; this is a regional system, not PAPSS.
